name: Autoimmune Polyglandular Syndrome

ethnicAssociations: Type 1 (APECED): Finnish, Sardinian, Iranian Jewish populations (higher prevalence)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for APS Type 1 and Type 2

criteria.description: Type 1 (APECED): Two of three cardinal features: chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, hypoparathyroidism, adrenal insufficiency (Addison's)
Type 1: One cardinal feature in a sibling of an affected individual
Type 2 (Schmidt syndrome): Adrenal insufficiency (Addison's) plus autoimmune thyroid disease (Hashimoto's or Graves') and/or Type 1 diabetes
Type 2: Presence of organ-specific autoantibodies supporting diagnosis
Type 3: Autoimmune thyroid disease plus another autoimmune condition (excluding adrenal insufficiency)
Type 4: Two or more organ-specific autoimmune endocrine conditions not fitting Types 1-3

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Type 1: 2 of 3 cardinal features OR 1 cardinal feature plus AIRE mutation OR 1 cardinal feature in sibling of APECED patient. Type 2: Addison's disease plus autoimmune thyroid disease and/or Type 1 diabetes.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Type 1 (APECED) is autosomal recessive (AIRE gene); onset in childhood. Type 2 (Schmidt) is polygenic with HLA associations; onset in adulthood. Type 2 is much more common than Type 1.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Combination of multiple endocrine autoimmune diseases
pathognomonic.notes: The hallmark is the co-occurrence of multiple autoimmune endocrinopathies
Usually first manifestation of APECED; onset in infancy/early childhood
Usually second manifestation of APECED; hypocalcemia

common.notes: Cardinal feature in both Type 1 and Type 2

occasional.symptomName: Nail dystrophy and dental enamel hypoplasia (Type 1)

laboratory: Organ-specific autoantibodies: 21-hydroxylase (adrenal), anti-TPO/TG (thyroid), anti-GAD/IA2/ZnT8 (islet), anti-parietal cell/intrinsic factor (gastric)
Anti-interferon-omega and anti-IL-22 antibodies (Type 1 APECED; highly sensitive and specific)
Low cortisol with elevated ACTH (adrenal insufficiency)
Hypocalcemia with low PTH (hypoparathyroidism in Type 1)
Low B12 with macrocytic anemia (pernicious anemia)
imaging: Thyroid ultrasound: features of Hashimoto's or Graves'
genetic: Type 1 (APECED): AIRE gene mutations (autosomal recessive; chromosome 21q22.3)
other: Regular screening for new autoimmune components (annual thyroid function, cortisol, glucose, B12, celiac antibodies, calcium/PTH)
Family screening in Type 1 (AIRE gene testing) and monitoring in Type 2

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated adrenal insufficiency without other endocrinopathies
May be early presentation of APS Type 2; screen for additional components
No adrenal or islet cell disease
May progress to APS if additional glands become affected
Screen for thyroid and adrenal antibodies to detect evolving APS

redFlags: Adrenal crisis in patient with known thyroid or diabetes autoimmunity (undiagnosed Addison's)
New endocrine organ failure in patient with existing autoimmune endocrine disease
Severe mucocutaneous candidiasis in childhood (APECED screening needed)
Autoimmune hepatitis in child with candidiasis (APECED - can be fatal)
references: Husebye ES, et al. Autoimmune polyendocrine syndromes. N Engl J Med. 2018;378(12):1132-1141.
Kahaly GJ. Polyglandular autoimmune syndromes. Eur J Endocrinol. 2009;161(1):11-20.
Betterle C, et al. Clinical review 93: Autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 1998;83(4):1049-1055.
